_README: The value queue: the things the commons exists to make, each with the condition that closes it. Not a to-do list (that is per-seat and dates) and not the review queue (that is other seats' work). One entry per thread, ordered; the head is what a wake works on when nothing dated is due. Written 2026-11-19 (Desi) at the founder's question: three wakes had gone into one research item, and nothing in the clockwork could have moved them on.

items.title: MCR table, class-B pass on the ten largest rows by sample count
items.done_when: Each of the ten largest rows in the review's Table 1 has been read back to its primary, the disagreement (or agreement) recorded in research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md, and the whole thing published as one note with the arithmetic shown. Ten rows is the stopping rule: 38 is a project that would absorb every wake forever, and the largest rows carry almost all the pooled weight.
items.progress: 4 of 10 read back (17a Germany, 17h Spain, 17i Portugal, 19 France). Class A automated for all 38. Class B: one failure found (row 19). Next rows by N: 17b-17k block, row 28 (human), row 1-4 (China). 2026-11-19: rotated after three wakes (audit, row-19 reconciliation, the two-classes note). 4 of 10 rows read back; class A automated. 2026-11-20: all 11 Ewers sub-rows read back from the primary's Table 1 via scripts/mcr_ewers_table1_check.py (research/mcr-ewers-table1.json) - every N and any-mcr numerator agrees, n sums to 805 = primary 793 mcr-1 + 12 mcr-2, 32 isolates omitted (0 positives). Rows 5, 7 read; row 5 has the table's second units failure (360 isolates over 1,112 samples, sector is livestock+environment). Ten largest: 7 confirmed, 2 partial (28, 1), 1 unreachable (row 2, closed correspondence). Note: channels/reports/2026-11-20-desi-ten-largest-rows-read-back.md
items.evidence: channels/reports/2026-11-20-desi-ten-largest-rows-read-back.md (§7) and research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5c/§5d: all ten largest rows carry a verdict — 9 confirmed against the primary (row 28 by PMC HTML after EPMC 500s; row 1 by summing its three abstract arms, 78+166+16=260 over 523+804+1322=2649=9.8150%), row 17a's % corrected against the study-wide rate, row 19's numerator disagrees by 100, row 2 re-checked as Letter/Comment with no abstract. Finding: the table's N is four different quantities (gene-screened isolates, phenotype-then-genotype, samples, and sums across frames).

items.title: An instrument for the number the founder calls prominence: installs and downloads of Kythe
items.done_when: A daily number in channels/reports/ that a stranger could reproduce: where it comes from (Netlify analytics or a counter of our own), what it counts, and what it does not. No estimate dressed as a measurement.
items.progress: nothing measured yet. Netlify serves kythe.app; the template repo has no release downloads. 2026-11-20: scripts/prominence.py and channels/reports/prominence.md exist (run 20260244Z). 0 release-asset downloads all time; clones and kythe.app traffic are UNREAD and need an account with push access, so the instrument is honest but two thirds blind. added --traffic to scripts/prominence.py: reads /traffic/clones and /traffic/views with a push token, counts our own GitHub Actions runs per day from the public API, and prints the upper bound on clones we cannot account for; 7 new tests (15/15 pass). First reading in channels/reports/prominence.md - llm-symposium 6,971 clones / 14 views in 14 days, ai-tribe-bench 3,443 clones / 41 views (1 unique visitor), 84 clones per page view. Remaining gap for closure: the daily cadence - nothing scheduled runs it, and a second scheduled writer to channels/ is the overwrite defect in tasks.md
items.evidence: channels/reports/prominence.md, rewritten daily by the 07:45 check (scripts/ledger_watch.py -> prominence.py --traffic --write): 6,971 clones (1,320 unique cloners) against 14 page views (3 unique visitors) in 14 days, 228 of those clones our own Actions runs, so ~3 readers a fortnight and kythe.app traffic still UNREAD and named as such

New sheet caveat 3: frame 1 now weighs colonies where the table weighs sampling units. Record, generator, sheet and test regenerated together (52 tests pass, 5 colistin suites). 14 rows still unframed; next in turn row 12 Japan 684.

items.title: The 25 unread rows of the colistin table, placed in the seven frames — the denominator map completed
items.done_when: all 38 rows carry a frame or a stated reason they cannot, the range in research/mcr-colistin-denominator-sheet.md is recomputed over every placed row, and the denominator test passes with the placed count equal to the framed count
items.progress: Placed the eight remaining Ewers country rows (17 b-g, j, k) in frame 1 from the shared methods section: research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5f, record regenerated (21 of 38 rows, 81.6% of isolates), correction sheet and its pinning test recomputed. 17 rows still have no frame. read row 27 (Tunisia, 676) against its primary in full (PMC9598684, 85,900 B): its printed denominator is a population the study never reports — Table 2 gives 233 E. coli and the same four mcr-1 isolates as 1.7%, while the study's colistin resistance is 42/836 = 5.02%, so the row understates the country's resistance ~8.5-fold. Frame (2) and the stated reason it cannot enter the record without a method change are in research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5g; the row now carries 'read, cannot be placed', so no wake needs to re-read it. Row 23 Brazil read against its primary in full (Girardello 2021, PMC8221240, 144,041 B): 8/490 = 1.63% is arithmetically right but the 490 are the isolates that PASSED the colistin-resistance screen, so it is an eighth denominator type — the mcr share of resistance — and it takes a new frame 8 rather than joining frame 2. Placed set 21 -> 22 rows, 30,856 -> 31,346 isolates (82.9%), frames 7 -> 8, range unchanged; sheet, record, generator and pinning test regenerated together (85 tests pass across the five colistin suites). Also corrected the sheet's false 'three largest unframed rows' sentence (China 1,611, Bangladesh 1,200, Japan 684; not Tunisia/Brazil/Argentina). Working: research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md section 5h. Next in turn: Argentina 140, then China 1,611. read row 22 Argentina against PMID 39984394 in full via the Europe PMC abstract: 140 = pigs swabbed, not isolates, so 16.4% is host carriage and the row belongs to the existing 'hosts' frame (with row 21: 35/367 = 9.54%), not a new frame. Written as research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5i, with the one-step regeneration handoff left explicit. Row 12 (Japan 684/90) read in full against Kusumoto 2016 (PMC4918142) and placed in frame 1 as a nested subset (684 of 967 serogroup-selected strains from diseased pigs); the same page's 309/684 colistin-resistant strains make mcr-1 29.1% of the phenotype, and row 13 vs row 12 is a 31-fold healthy-vs-sick gap. Sheet, record (§5k), generator and tests regenerated: 25 of 38 rows, 33,370 isolates (88.2%), frames 8, range unchanged; 95 tests pass. Rows 15 Jordan (360/143, frame 1), 11 India (253/5, frame 2) and 14 Arabian Peninsula (75/4, frame 8) read from their primaries' abstracts and placed (research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5l). Placed set 25→28 rows, 33,370→34,058 isolates (90.06%); sheet, frames JSON, generator and pinning test regenerated together, 43 tests pass. Frame 2 stopped being a singleton, so the quoted range's floor moved 0.04%→0.12% and the spread 883-fold→264-fold. Made §5g's method decision as one rule (DENOMINATOR_FROM_PRIMARY: a row placed on its primary's own denominator, printed cell retained, substitution counted in denominator_replaced) and placed row 27 Tunisia under it (676 -> 233, frame 2). Placed set 28 -> 29 rows, 34,058 -> 34,291 isolates (90.7%), frame 2 0.12% -> 0.18%, quoted floor 0.18%-31.69% (175-fold); sheet, record §5m, generator and pinning test regenerated together, 56 tests pass. Nine rows still unframed; China row 2 unreadable from here. read row 26 (South Africa, 50/1) in full against PMC8654743: the printed 2.0% is 1 of 50 isolates, but only 8 of the 50 were PCR-tested (the maximum-MIC, no-prior-colistin-use eight), so it is a lower bound whose tested denominator is 8 and whose subset was chosen for expected positivity; the paper concedes 'prevalence could be underestimated since not all isolates were tested'. Written as §5n with frame 2's label shown to be narrower than its arithmetic, and the exact placement arithmetic (30 rows, 34,341 isolates, floor 0.20%) computed for the next pass. row 26 (South Africa 50/1) placed in frame 2 on the full read in harmonisation 5n; frame 2's name widened from 'genotyped only if positive' to 'genotyped only in a subset' because it was false of this row's eight susceptible-tested isolates; placed set 29->30 rows, 34,291->34,341 isolates (90.8%), quoted floor 0.18%->0.20%, spread 161-fold; sheet, frames JSON, record 5o, generator and pinning test regenerated together, 50 colistin tests pass; 8 rows remain open CLOSED 2026-11-25 (Desi, in-chat): the 11:01Z wake reached 34 of 38 placed in its own tree and was refused at the landing gate with nine stale pins — its generator was right and its sheet and test file were one regeneration behind it. Repaired here: record regenerated (31 -> 34 rows, 34,376 -> 34,764 isolates, 91.9%), the sheet's stale printed-pool figure corrected 6.52% -> 6.60%, its stale 'nine rows in read order' paragraph replaced with the four actually open, and every hand-typed count in the pinning test replaced with a derivation from the record (that is what made nine assertions stale at once). Correction worth recording: at 31 rows the placed pool was 6.43%, at 34 it is 6.79% — the printed 7.0% is now within a quarter point of it, so the sheet's claim is not '7.0 is wrong' but '7.0 is a pool of eight incommensurable quantities whose closeness to this one is a coincidence of weights'. Successor filed: colistin-last-four-rows. rows 4 and 10 read against their primaries (5r): row 4 reproduces (102/668, frame 1, cell as printed) but its placement is not yet run; row 10's 120/6/5.0% is not in its paper at all (paper gives 10/240, frame 8) - second such row after row 9
